name: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions
principle: Code omits or performs the wrong check for rare failure conditions such as allocation failure, permission failure, resource exhaustion, invalid status, or misbehaving components. Attackers can trigger these paths so the program continues with invalid state, crashes, or exposes unsafe behavior.
detection_signals: malloc/calloc/realloc/new result dereferenced before NULL/nullptr check
fopen/open/socket/accept/connect result used before checking NULL or negative return
read/write/recv/send return value ignored or not compared with requested byte count
setuid/setgid/chroot/setrlimit return value ignored before privileged or security-sensitive operation
Java method that can throw IOException/SQLException/GeneralSecurityException called without local handling or propagation policy
catch (Exception e) or catch (...) block that continues using state produced inside the try block
status/error enum compared only to one success value while other documented unusual statuses fall through as success
negative_signals: failure-capable call immediately followed by if (ret < 0), if (ptr == NULL), or equivalent guard before use
partial I/O loop handles EINTR/EAGAIN and short read/write counts explicitly
Java try/catch catches specific checked exceptions and returns, retries, rolls back, or propagates a typed error
RAII wrapper or smart pointer constructor throws and caller catches specific allocation/resource exception
error path clears or invalidates output variables before returning failure
false_defense_traps: assert(ptr != NULL) used as the only runtime check
catch (Exception) logs the error but continues normal processing
checking only errno without first checking the failing return value
checking for NULL after the pointer has already been dereferenced
system limits configured but low-resource failure paths still unhandled
verification_focus: Does every operation that can fail have a correct check before its outputs, privileges, resources, or state are trusted?

consequence_chains.trigger: allocation or lookup returns NULL and code dereferences the result
return value is checked but resource state changes before use in concurrent code
consequence_chains.consequence: unexpected state or unsafe operation on stale assumptions

consequence_chains.trigger: exceptional condition is handled by returning detailed internal error text to the user
consequence_chains.consequence: information exposure that helps refine attacks

patch_principle: Check every failure-capable return value before using outputs or continuing control flow.
Handle each documented exceptional status explicitly with return, retry, rollback, or fail-closed behavior.
Catch and throw specific exceptions instead of broad catch-all handlers.
Keep error details minimal for users and place sensitive diagnostics only in protected logs.
Design low-resource and permission-denied paths to leave state consistent.

minimal_examples.safe: char *buf = malloc(n); if (buf == NULL) return -1; buf[0] = '\0';
